For me, Geometry Dash stopped being "just a rhythm game" a long time ago. Past a certain point, it turns into less of a game and more of a test of patience, consistency, and mental fortitude.

When I first bought it, I genuinely thought it was just a simple cube game with music playing in the background. After playing a few easy levels, I realized how wrong I was. The deeper you get into Geometry Dash, the better you understand why people sink thousands of hours into this game.

Right now, I’m at a level where I can consistently beat Hard Demons, and even this has completely shifted my perspective on the game. Levels no longer feel like random obstacles; it becomes a matter of muscle memory, timing, reflex control, and pure focus. You start recognizing patterns instantly, developing click consistency, understanding the sync better, and learning something from almost every single death. To an outsider, it might look like mindless repetition, but when you’re actually playing, every attempt feels like progress in some way.

The game's difficulty is brutal, but weirdly enough, it feels fair. Most of the time when you die, you know EXACTLY why you died. Maybe you panicked, clicked too early, lost focus for a split second, or choked because you got nervous near the end. And the strange thing is, that’s precisely what makes beating a difficult level so satisfying.

The only other game in my life that ever gave me this feeling was Elden Ring. That sensation of grinding for hours and finally overcoming something that seemed impossible... But to be honest, Geometry Dash makes me feel it even more intensely. Because here, there is absolutely nothing else to blame. No RNG, no teammates, no excuses — it’s just you, your reflexes, your consistency, and your own mistakes. Every new best you hit, every percentage you gain, and every completion you pull off feels truly earned.
One of the biggest reasons this game is still so alive after all these years is its community. The level editor is, honestly, insane. People create cinematic levels, boss fights, impossible challenges, memory demons, modern art-style levels, and effect levels that look like they shouldn't even be possible in this game.

The music gets way less credit than it deserves, too. After playing enough, certain songs become directly tied to specific levels, fails, progress memories, and that feeling of victory. Sometimes I’ll hear a song outside of the game, and the click patterns of a level will instantly pop into my head.

And honestly, one of the best parts about Geometry Dash is actually being able to see your own improvement. You don’t notice it at first, but one day you go back to a level that used to seem impossible, and suddenly, it feels easy. That feeling is extremely addictive.

Yes, the game is frustrating.
Yes, it can break your mentality.
Yes, when you say "one last attempt," it's never actually the last attempt.

But very few games can make self-improvement feel this real.

It requires a lot of patience to beat demons but the excitement and happiness you feel when you do so is more than worth it. After playing this game for 2000 hours on Steam, not counting many hours spent on mobile versions, I can confidently say that Geometry Dash is my favourite game of all time.

I love this game for 5 main reasons:

[olist]
    [*]Simple gameplay with high stakes, as your character moves through the levels automatically and you only need to control when it jumps, but if it hits just one obstacle, it dies and you have to restart the level from the very beginning! This creates a frustrating yet addictive experience, and it makes you want to try and try again, because you know where you messed up, and since the gameplay is so basic, you know what to do next time to get a little further into the level! Besides that, the game has a lot of level objects, from orbs that make you jump in the air when you click them, portals that change character's gravity and speed, to different character gamemodes, which change their jump to flight, switching gravity, teleporting and so on, and it all makes the gameplay fresh in every level so you won't get bored.
    [*]Strong sense of progression, because in a hard game such as this, you will clearly see your growth in skill, not in basic statistic, but in the levels you completed. At first, you are going to complete the easiest of levels, but eventually you'll move onto harder and harder ones. You will notice then how much confidence you have to complete the levels you previously feared. This brings a truly satisfying feeling, more than simply completing a game - you become skilled and confident enough to take on harder challenges. This sense of progression is further supported by showing you the amount of stars and demons, the hardest levels of the game, on your account. Additionaly, many icons for your character can only be unlocked by completing harder challenges, and by seeing how many icons you unlocked, you can see how far you've come in this simple game about jumping over spikes. 
    [*]Amazing level editor, which is THE selling point of Geometry Dash! This is the thing that gives truly limitless potential for the game, as I believe this is one of the best level editors in the game industry. Any object can be moved to any part of the grid, any object can be rotated to any degree you'd like, and any object can even be scaled by X and Y axis. This gives you a lot of potential for decoration in your levels! Besides that, level editor lets you place triggers, which manipulate the level in different ways. They can do something simple, like move objects or change their colors, and can do something drastic, like check collision or remember certain data. Triggers are what allow determined creators to change the level from a simple autoscroller to different game genres! And just when you think it can't get any better, the editor allows to use a vast majority of songs to be played in the level, like music from popular creative website Newgrounds.com, music from popular electronic music label NoCopyrightSounds, and a large music library from songs of various music composers! There are certain limits to this level editor, but as the creators push the limits of the game, the editor expands every update, bringing new features to create unbelievable levels!
    [*]Passionate community, because a good level editor isn't the only ingredient for a timeless game. Without the passionate community, that learned how to push the game and it's level editor to the limits, GD wouldn’t have come so far! This community is truly amazing, continuously supporting the game by creating artistic masterpieces, that sync with the song perfectly, that have beautiful decorations, and that have fun gameplay. Yeah, not all levels are this perfect, and you will find yourself disagreeing with many players, but this doesn't take away from the fact that this community loves the game very much to still keep it alive. Not only the creator side of the community is awesome, a big part of the playerbase are challenging themselves to the hardest levels in the game, which keeps raising the bar of difficulty of this already hard game!  
    [*]Passionate creator, Robert Topala, who has been working on this game all by himself since 2013, clearly showing how much he loves his game and its community. Not only is he working on the game itself, he continuously supports it by rating new community levels, running creator contests and sometimes interacting with the community directly. RobTop really is my favourite game developer, and he is a living proof that you can have a successful and fulfilling life by creating a game that everybody likes, which inspires me to try and become a game developer myself.
[/olist]

However, Geometry Dash is not perfect, like any other game. It has some significant flaws, like security issues, many bugs ranging from annoying to gamebreaking, outdated rating system, and, worst of all, slow updates. And yet, most of these problems could be fixed if RobTop hired more people to work on the game and didn’t have to do it alone.

I know I just praised RobTop for being so passionate about his game, but the problem is, he’s just one developer. GD is way bigger now than it used to be years ago, and it’s obvious that RobTop struggles to have time for everything. I hope one day he will realise that him working alone will mostly harm his game in the long run.

Nevertheless, these flaws don’t ruin the game at all, as in my experience they rarely mattered. And when you don't encounter them, you get a game with limitless amount of artistic and challenging levels for just $4.99! You don't need to purchase any extra dlc or microtransactions to get the full experience, and that in my opinion makes Geometry Dash one of the best deals on the market!

Finally, Geometry Dash means a lot to me personally. Ever since childhood, this game has caught my attention, when me and my classmates were very engaged with this game on our mobile devices and all tried to complete the main levels for glory! And after all this time, after I grew up, finished school and went to university, this game is still with me, still mostly the same, but growing, just like me. And I still find people who play Geometry Dash together on their mobile devices, continuing the trend of beating the levels for glory in their class. Seeing this makes me smile everytime, because I remember that Geometry Dash is still alive and well even after 12 years already, and not going to die anytime soon!

So thank you, Geometry Dash! Thank you for everything that you've done for my life :)

I have put around 350 hours into Geometry Dash. It is easily one of the most satisfying games I have ever played. On the surface its just dodging spikes, but in reality it is about self-improvement. Every attempt teaches you something. Every death forces you to adapt, Every completion feels genuinely earned.

The music is peak, like, unimaginably peak, because u have almost the entirety of newgrounds in your reach. The levels look incredible and even a 1% improvement in progress hits like morning brizz. 

One of my achievements was beating Bloodbath. After a 99% fail at Bloodbath I was beyond frustrated, but I reminded myself that if I could get to there once, I could get there again. That mindset carried me through gd. I never truly gave up, evemn when the levels destroyed my sanity one attempt at a time. Small improvements in consistency slowly built my confidence until I reached a point where I felt like I could beat it on any attempt. And eventually I did.

It took 5 months and around 25000 attempts to beat Bloodbath. It was a jump in difficulty going from Ultra Violence (Medium Demon) to a Top 670 extreme. My long-term goal is to beat Slaughterhouse, a 20 demon in Geometry Dash. Sure it might take years, but who cares, i got time. This game teaches you something important: no matter how impossible something feels, progress is always there if you just keep going.

As mentioned before, the music is peak, and the levels are beautiful. The level editor is basically a full game engine. Actually playing it feels surreal and insanely rewarding.

10/10 Would die to spikes again.

777.7 Hours Played. Progress Update

At 777.7 hours, It feels like a different game compared to when I first started playing It. What used to feel impossible now feels manageable. What used to feel hard is now just warm-up. The grind does not go away. You just get better at handling It.

My skillset has changed a lot too. I have become heavily wave/spam-carried. And that has changed the way I approach levels. Fast precise high-control gameplay is where I am most consistent now. Consistency matters more than raw skill at this point. It is not about "can I do this once" ,it is about "can I do this every time it matters" . That is where the real difficulty of gd shows itself.

Over this time, I have Achieved many things on many levels:

Cataclysm 100%, fluke from 60
Acu 100%, almost fluked but died to the last triple spike twice
Trip 100%, had to master the triple spike bc i died to it both in bb and acu
Sweater Weather 100%, , fluke from 51
Aftermath 100%, fluke from 37
Shitty Grief 39%, 25-67, 65-95
Almost did the USKC spam
Grief 0-76 in 99 deaths, griefer in 2, and tacos in 11
Zodiac 39%, 60-100 in 3 deaths
Acheron 19%, 59-100 in 10 deaths, 81-100 in 1
And most importantly, Slaughterhouse 25%, 25-55, 50-61 and 62-94(basically SLH in 4 runs, im only missing like 3 clicks)

When u have progress on so many levels, its hard to choose ur next hardest. I will probably jump yet again from bb to Zodiac, following zoink's footprints. Then jump from Zodiac to SLH. It's crazy how my hardest is still bb, despite the fact that my playtime has doubled, but I'm not ashamed of it. These 777 hours include at least 100 hours of afk and 120 hours of noclip levels, which i am proud to admit bc its fun. 

This game never get's boring, even when my finger hurts from high cps, I keep going, which is why this will always be 10/10 game for me.

[b] MY THOUGHTS [/b]

I really do think Geometry Dash doesn't deserve the rep it gets; the game is quite enjoyable. However, I would not recommend it to anyone who has difficulty sitting down and trying to accomplish one thing at a time. 

The game is very easy to be viewed by others, but when actually being played poses huge amounts of difficulty that quite frankly is outrageous. You saw Npesta beat Kenos and go crazy (the one guy who went viral with his reaction to beating a level). Many, including myself initially probably thought about how crazy of a reaction he had to just a game. Yet his reaction might as well be the best explanation to what this game really is: lots of hard, tireless work into just a single level of hundreds of thousands. To beat any level in this game with lots of effort is something that many like me find quite enjoyable; it's like trying your hardest to be the best at something and coming at the top, a feeling that I feel is quite underrepresented in today's games. 

And oh man, the audio of this game might be one of my favorite. Geometry Dash songs are all sourced from Newgrounds to avoid copyright issues. Some of my favorite techno, remixes, and electronic songs came from this game. Sound's crazy right? A level in this game could not be a level without fitting audio to match a levels template and mood.

Levels can have varying graphics from the most boring simple layout to literally a short CGI movie. Some levels like to blind their players (quite literally), others like to keep it classy with some exceptionally thought-out layouts.

As I write this, I have beaten both Clubstep and Deadlocked with only 10 hours in this game, which might seem suspicious, yet is justified in that I had already played this game on mobile (with far more attempts lol).


[b] CONS [/b]

I would take away how there really isn't any integration via steam and instead through the Boomlings website, meaning that game data is not stored on Steam. Also, you have to save your progress yourself instead of the progress being automatically saved to your account. 

Another issue that I don't see being resolved is how the difference in the hertz of your monitor can affect gameplay, where sometimes the hertz in your monitor can break a level or make it easier. 

A very code-based issue that I think is being addressed somewhat by the moderators in the game itself is the level of how easy it is to cheat in this game. Many often are banned, but there are a few that are very popular that get away with it. I don't see this being an issue ever being resolved as this would require many changes in the code of the game.

My final concern is with the lack of updates; the recent update was well over 3 years ago now (which hopefully is changing soon with the new sneak peek for 2.2). 

[b] CONCLUSION [/b]

With all this being said, this game is an 9.25/10. There are many issues that need to be addressed for this game to reach its full potential, but in terms of gameplay and my enjoyment, there is a lot of stuff made up for in its flaws. It's well worth just the $4 I and many others spent on this game.

I have been playing Geometry Dash for over 7 years now, and in those 7 years I have done a lot. Beating continually harder levels, creating levels, and completing goals that I set for myself all make this game impeccable.

On the surface, it's an incredibly basic game, you click, and you jump... That is it. But what makes this game special is the level editor, where people can make their own levels and complete levels made by others, and it's the only reason this game lasted for 7 years without an update.

The base game consists of 22 levels, with new levels added with each update.  And most players can probably beat all of them in a few months of playing, so what's next? The community made levels. As of writing this, there are over 111,000,000 custom levels. Yes, 111 MILLION. There are so many, that it is physically impossible to beat every single one.

There are 10 tiers of difficulties that I will list off now:
- Auto - These levels are completely automatic, you can beat them without clicking.
- Easy - These levels are borderline automatic, and have very simple gameplay.
- Normal - These levels have more advanced gameplay, but are often still relatively easy.
- Hard - These are the average levels, and you'll often fail multiple times before beating them.
- Harder - These are Hard levels, just a bit harder.
- Insane - These levels are relatively hard, and you will fail many times before beating them.
- Easy Demon - The first of the five demon difficulties, these are NOT to be underestimated, and they will take many, many fails to complete. I personally spent 3 years playing the game before completing my first one.
- Medium Demon - These are a fair amount harder than Easy Demons, and will probably take a lot longer to beat.
- Hard Demon - These demons are the default demon difficulty, and feel rewarding to beat.
- Insane Demon - These are some of the hardest levels in the game, and beating one is not an easy task.
- Extreme Demon - These are the hardest levels in the game, and it will be a long time before you beat one. I only beat my first one this year (2024) and I spent close to 17,000 attempts on it. The difficulty of extreme demons vary and some are a lot harder than others.

Each of these will give you a different reward amount, Auto levels for example give only 1 star, while every demon difficulty gives 10.

Overall, Geometry Dash isn't a game for everyone, but if you are looking for a challenge (and maybe a headache), try it out.
